drills.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at {v0} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its maximum height above the launch point and its total time in the air (until it returns to the launch height), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
At the top $v_y = 0$: $0 = {v0}^2 - 2(9.8)H$, so $H =$ **{H:sig3} m**.

Time up $= {v0}/9.8$ s; time down is the same, so $T = 2({v0})/9.8 =$ **{T:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Horizontal launch from a height
drills.prompt: A ball leaves the edge of a {h} m high ledge moving horizontally at {v} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², how far from the base of the ledge does it land, and what is its speed just before landing? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Fall time from the vertical motion: $t = \sqrt{2h/g} = \sqrt{2({h})/9.8} = {t:sig3}$ s.

Horizontal distance: $x = v t = {v}({t:sig3}) =$ **{x:sig3} m**.

At impact $v_y = gt = {vy:num2}$ m/s, so speed $= \sqrt{{v}^2 + {vy:num2}^2} =$ **{s:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Range, height and flight time on level ground
drills.prompt: A ball is launched from level ground at {v0} m/s, {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the time of flight, the maximum height and the range, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v_{0x} = {v0}\cos {th}^\circ = {vx:num2}$ m/s, $v_{0y} = {v0}\sin {th}^\circ = {vy:num2}$ m/s.

$T = 2v_{0y}/g =$ **{T:sig3} s**; $H = v_{0y}^2/(2g) =$ **{H:sig3} m**; $R = v_{0x}T = \dfrac{v_0^2\sin 2\theta}{g} =$ **{R:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Crossing a river
drills.prompt: A river {w} m wide flows at {vc} m/s. A boat moves at {vs} m/s relative to the water. (a) Heading straight across, how far downstream does it land? (b) To land directly opposite, how many degrees upstream from straight across must it head? Give the drift to 3 significant figures and the angle to the nearest 0.1°.
drills.solution:
(a) Crossing time uses only the across component: $t = {w}/{vs} = {t:num2}$ s. Drift $= {vc} \times {t:num2} =$ **{drift:sig3} m**.

(b) The upstream component must cancel the current: ${vs}\sin\alpha = {vc}$, so $\alpha = \sin^{-1}({vc}/{vs}) =$ **{ang:num1}°**.

drills.title: Airplane in a crosswind
drills.prompt: A plane with airspeed {va} km/h must fly due north while a wind blows toward the east at {vw} km/h. How many degrees west of north must it head, and what is its ground speed? Give the heading to the nearest 0.1° and the ground speed to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\vec v_{PG} = \vec v_{PA} + \vec v_{AG}$. The plane's eastward airspeed component must be $-{vw}$ km/h: ${va}\sin\alpha = {vw}$, so $\alpha =$ **{head:num1}°** west of north.

Ground speed $= {va}\cos\alpha = \sqrt{{va}^2 - {vw}^2} =$ **{vg:sig3} km/h**.

drills.title: Velocity and speed from a position vector
drills.prompt: A particle's position is $\vec r(t) = ({a:coef}t^2)\,\hat\imath + ({b}t - {c:coef}t^3)\,\hat\jmath$ in meters. Find $v_x$ and $v_y$ (exact values) and the speed (to 3 significant figures) at $t = {t}$ s.
drills.solution:
$\vec v = \dfrac{d\vec r}{dt} = ({a2}t)\,\hat\imath + ({b} - {c3}t^2)\,\hat\jmath$.

At $t = {t}$: $v_x =$ **{vx} m/s**, $v_y =$ **{vy} m/s**, speed $= \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} =$ **{sp:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Acceleration with an angled pull
drills.prompt: A {m} kg sled on frictionless ice is pulled by a rope with tension {F} N at {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the sled's acceleration and the normal force on it. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Horizontal: ${F}\cos {th}^\circ = {m}a$, so $a =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

Vertical ($a_y = 0$): $n + {F}\sin {th}^\circ - {m}(9.8) = 0$, so $n =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Apparent weight in an elevator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg person stands on a scale in an elevator accelerating {dir} at {acc} m/s². What does the scale read? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The scale reads the normal force. With up positive, $n - mg = ma$, where $a = +{acc}$ m/s² if the acceleration is upward and $-{acc}$ m/s² if downward.

Acceleration is {dir}, so $a = {sa}$ m/s² and $n = m(g + a) = {m}(9.8 + ({sa})) =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Net force from two perpendicular forces
drills.prompt: Two horizontal forces act on a {m} kg puck on frictionless ice: {F1} N east and {F2} N north. Find the magnitude of its acceleration and its direction in degrees north of east. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{{F1}^2 + {F2}^2} = {Fn:num2}$ N, so $a = F_{\text{net}}/m = {Fn:num2}/{m} =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

Direction: $\tan^{-1}({F2}/{F1}) =$ **{ang:sig3}°** north of east (the acceleration points along the net force).

drills.title: Block on a frictionless incline
drills.prompt: A block is released from rest on a frictionless ramp inclined at {th}°. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its acceleration and its speed after sliding {L} m along the ramp. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Along the slope only $mg\sin\theta$ acts: $a = g\sin\theta = 9.8\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$v^2 = 2aL$, so $v = \sqrt{2({a:num2})({L})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Sliding down an incline with friction
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block slides down a {th}° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is {mu}. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the friction force and the block's acceleration. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$n = mg\cos\theta = {m}(9.8)\cos {th}^\circ$, so $f_k = \mu_k n =$ **{f:sig3} N** (up the slope).

$a = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta) = 9.8(\sin {th}^\circ - {mu}\cos {th}^\circ) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²** down the slope.

drills.title: Force needed to start a box moving
drills.prompt: A {m} kg box rests on a level floor with $\mu_s = {ms}$ and $\mu_k = {mk}$. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the smallest horizontal force that starts it moving, and its acceleration if that same force keeps pushing once it slides. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$n = mg = {m}(9.8)$ N. Maximum static friction: $\mu_s n =$ **{Fs:sig3} N**, the force needed to start it.

Sliding: $f_k = \mu_k n$, so $a = \dfrac{\mu_s n - \mu_k n}{\,m} = (\mu_s - \mu_k)g =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

drills.title: Atwood machine
drills.prompt: Masses of {m1} kg and {m2} kg hang on either side of an ideal pulley. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the magnitude of their acceleration and the tension in the rope. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Heavier side down: ${m1}g - T = {m1}a$ and $T - {m2}g = {m2}a$. Adding:

$a = \dfrac{{m1} - {m2}}{{m1} + {m2}}(9.8) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = {m2}(g + a) = \dfrac{2m_1m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Block on a table pulled by a hanging mass
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg block on a horizontal table ($\mu_k = {mu}$) is tied by a rope over an ideal pulley to a hanging {m2} kg mass. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the acceleration and the tension. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Table block: $T - \mu_k m_1 g = m_1 a$. Hanging mass: $m_2 g - T = m_2 a$. Adding:

$a = \dfrac{m_2 - \mu_k m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g = \dfrac{{m2} - ({mu})({m1})}{{m1} + {m2}}(9.8) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = m_2(g - a) =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Tension in two symmetric cables
drills.prompt: A {m} kg sign hangs at rest from two cables, each making {th}° with the horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the tension in each cable. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Horizontal components cancel by symmetry. Vertically, $2T\sin\theta = mg$:

$T = \dfrac{{m}(9.8)}{2\sin {th}^\circ} =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Centripetal acceleration and force
drills.prompt: A {m} kg ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle of radius {r} m on a frictionless table, completing one revolution every {T} s. Find its speed, its centripetal acceleration and the string tension. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v = 2\pi r/T = 2\pi({r})/{T} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$a_c = v^2/r =$ **{ac:sig3} m/s²**, toward the center.

The string supplies the inward force: $T_{\text{string}} = ma_c =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Maximum speed on a flat curve
drills.prompt: What is the maximum speed at which a car can round a flat curve of radius {r} m if the coefficient of static friction between tires and road is {mu}? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² and answer in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Static friction supplies the inward force: $\mu_s mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{\,r}$, so

$v = \sqrt{\mu_s g r} = \sqrt{({mu})(9.8)({r})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s** (about {kmh:num1} km/h). The mass cancels.

drills.title: Vertical loop
drills.prompt: A roller coaster loop has radius {r} m. (a) What minimum speed must a car have at the top to stay on the track? (b) A {m} kg rider passes the bottom at {vb} m/s; what normal force does the seat exert on her there? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) At the limit $n = 0$ and gravity alone gives the inward force: $mg = mv^2/r$, so $v_{\min} = \sqrt{gr} =$ **{vmin:sig3} m/s**.

(b) At the bottom the net force is upward: $n - mg = mv^2/r$, so $n = {m}(9.8) + \dfrac{{m}({vb})^2}{{r}} =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Work done by an angled force and by friction
drills.prompt: A crate is dragged {d} m across a level floor by a rope with tension {F} N at {th}° above horizontal. Kinetic friction on the crate is {f} N. Find the work done by the rope, the work done by friction (with its sign), and the net work, in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Rope: $W = Fd\cos\theta = {F}({d})\cos {th}^\circ =$ **{WF:sig3} J**.

Friction opposes the motion ($\theta = 180^\circ$): $W = -{f}({d}) =$ **{Wf} J**.

Gravity and the normal force are perpendicular to the motion and do no work, so $W_{\text{net}} =$ **{Wnet:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Work–energy theorem
drills.prompt: A {m} kg cart moving at {v0} m/s is pushed {d} m by a constant net force of {F} N in its direction of motion. Use the work–energy theorem to find its final speed in m/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$W_{\text{net}} = Fd = {F}({d}) = {W:dp0}$ J $= \tfrac12mv_f^2 - \tfrac12mv_i^2$.

$v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + 2W/m} = \sqrt{{v0}^2 + 2({W:dp0})/{m}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spring force and stored energy
drills.prompt: A spring with spring constant {k} N/m is stretched {xcm} cm from its natural length. What force does it exert (N), and how much work (J) was needed to stretch it? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Hooke's law: $|F| = kx = {k:dp0}({x}) =$ **{F:sig3} N** (pulling back toward equilibrium).

Work = area under the $F$–$x$ line $= \tfrac12kx^2 = \tfrac12({k:dp0})({x})^2 =$ **{U:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Speed at the bottom of a ramp (with and without friction)
drills.prompt: A {m} kg box starts from rest at the top of a ramp {h} m high. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find (a) its speed at the bottom if the ramp is frictionless, and (b) its speed if friction removes {pct}% of its initial potential energy. Give speeds in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $mgh = \tfrac12mv^2$, so $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({h})} =$ **{v0:sig3} m/s**.

(b) Friction removes {pct}% of $mgh$, so $\tfrac12mv^2 = (1 - {pct}/100)\,mgh$ and $v =$ **{v1:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spring launcher
drills.prompt: A spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m is compressed {xcm} cm and launches a {mg} g ball straight up. Ignoring air resistance and using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the ball's speed as it leaves the spring (neglect the small height change during launch) and the maximum height it reaches above the release point. Give the speed in m/s and the height in m, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Stored energy: $\tfrac12kx^2 = \tfrac12({k:dp0})({x})^2 = {U:num4}$ J.

Launch speed: $\tfrac12mv^2 = {U:num4}$ J with $m = {m}$ kg, so $v =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

Max height: $mgh = {U:num4}$ J, so $h = \dfrac{{U:num4}}{({m})(9.8)} =$ **{h:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Power to lift a load
drills.prompt: A motor lifts a {m} kg load {h} m at constant speed in {t} s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the power delivered to the load and, if the motor is {eff}% efficient, the electrical power it draws, in watts to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Work against gravity: $mgh = {m:dp0}(9.8)({h})$ J. $P = \dfrac{mgh}{\,t} =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

Input: $P_{\text{in}} = P/\eta = P/{eff}\% =$ **{Pin:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Impulse and average force in a rebound
drills.prompt: A {mg} g ball hits a wall at {v1} m/s and rebounds straight back at {v2} m/s. The contact lasts {tms} ms. Find the magnitude of the impulse (N·s) and of the average force on the ball (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Rebound direction positive: $\Delta p = m(v_f - v_i) = {m}({v2} - (-{v1})) =$ **{J:sig3} N·s**.

$F_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{{J:num4}}{{tms}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Recoil (momentum from rest)
drills.prompt: A {M} kg person standing on frictionless ice throws a {m} kg package horizontally at {v} m/s. With what speed does the person recoil? Give m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: ${m}({v}) + {M}V = 0$.

$|V| = \dfrac{{m}({v})}{{M}} =$ **{V:sig3} m/s**, opposite to the throw.

drills.title: Center of mass of three particles
drills.prompt: Find the center of mass of {m1} kg at $({x1}, {y1})$, {m2} kg at $({x2}, {y2})$ and {m3} kg at $({x3}, {y3})$ (coordinates in meters). Give each coordinate in meters to 2 decimal places.

drills.title: Perfectly inelastic collision
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg car moving at {v1} m/s collides with a {m2} kg car moving at {v2} m/s along the same line (negative means the opposite direction), and they lock together. Find their common velocity (m/s, with sign) and the kinetic energy lost (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Momentum: ${m1:dp0}({v1}) + {m2:dp0}({v2}) = ({m1:dp0} + {m2:dp0})v_f$, so $v_f =$ **{vf:sig3} m/s**.

$K_i = {Ki:dp0}$ J and $K_f = \tfrac12({Mt:dp0})v_f^2 = {Kf:dp0}$ J, so the loss is $K_i - K_f =$ **{dK:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Elastic collision with a target at rest
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg cart moving at {v} m/s collides head-on and elastically with a {m2} kg cart at rest. Find both final velocities in m/s, to 3 significant figures (positive = original direction of motion).
drills.solution:
$v_{1f} = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} = \dfrac{{m1} - {m2}}{{m1} + {m2}}({v}) =$ **{v1f:sig3} m/s**

$v_{2f} = \dfrac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} =$ **{v2f:sig3} m/s**

Check: they separate at $v_{2f} - v_{1f} = \dfrac{2m_1 - (m_1 - m_2)}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} = v_{1i} = {v}$ m/s, the same as the approach speed.

drills.title: Ballistic pendulum
drills.prompt: A {mg} g bullet embeds itself in a {M} kg block hanging from strings. The block swings up {hcm} cm. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the block's speed just after impact and the bullet's initial speed, in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Swing (energy conserved): $V = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({hcm}/100)} =$ **{V:sig3} m/s**.

Collision (momentum conserved): $mv = (m + M)V$, so $v = \dfrac{{m:dp3} + {M}}{{m:dp3}}({V:num4}) =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: The rocket equation and thrust
drills.prompt: A rocket of initial mass {mi} t (1 t = 1000 kg) in deep space ejects exhaust at {u} km/s relative to the rocket, at a rate of {R:dp0} kg/s, until it has burned fuel equal to {pct}% of its initial mass. Find its thrust (N), how long the burn lasts (s), and the speed it gains (km/s), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Thrust $= u\,|dm/dt| = ({u}\times10^{3})({R:dp0}) = \mathbf{{thrust:texsci}}$ N.

The final mass is $m_f = {mi}(1 - {pct}/100) = {mf:sig4}$ t, so the burn uses ${mi} - {mf:sig4}$ t of fuel and lasts **{tb:sig3} s** at {R:dp0} kg/s.

$\Delta v = u\ln\dfrac{m_i}{m_f} = {u}\ln\dfrac{{mi}}{{mf:sig4}} =$ **{dv:sig3} km/s**.

drills.title: Spinning down with constant angular acceleration
drills.prompt: A wheel spinning at {rpm} rpm slows uniformly to rest in {t} s. Find its angular acceleration (rad/s², with sign) and the number of revolutions it makes while stopping, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w0:num2}$ rad/s.

$\alpha = \dfrac{0 - \omega_0}{\,t} =$ **{alpha:sig3} rad/s²**.

$\Delta\theta = \tfrac12(\omega_0 + 0)t = {th:dp1}$ rad $=$ **{rev:sig3} rev**.

drills.title: Moment of inertia of masses on a rod
drills.prompt: A uniform rod of mass {M} kg and length {L} m has a small {m1} kg mass at its left end and a {m2} kg mass at its right end. Find the moment of inertia about (a) a perpendicular axis through the rod's center and (b) a perpendicular axis through the left end. Give kg·m² to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) Rod: $\tfrac1{12}ML^2$; each end mass is $L/2$ away: $I = \tfrac1{12}({M})({L})^2 + ({m1} + {m2})({L}/2)^2 =$ **{Ic:sig3} kg·m²**.

(b) Rod about an end: $\tfrac13ML^2$; the left mass is on the axis, the right mass is $L$ away: $I = \tfrac13({M})({L})^2 + {m2}({L})^2 =$ **{Ie:sig3} kg·m²**.

drills.title: Rotational kinetic energy of a disk
drills.prompt: A {M} kg {shape} of radius {R} m spins about its central axis at {rpm} rpm. Find its moment of inertia (kg·m²) and its rotational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
For a {shape}, $I = cMR^2$ with $c = {shape:num1}$, so $I =$ **{I:sig3} kg·m²**.

$\omega = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w:num2}$ rad/s, so $K = \tfrac12I\omega^2 =$ **{K:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Torque from an angled force
drills.prompt: A force of {F} N is applied at the end of a {r} m wrench, making an angle of {th}° with the handle. Find the torque about the bolt, and the maximum torque that force could produce, in N·m to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\tau = rF\sin\theta = ({r})({F})\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{tau:sig3} N·m**.

The maximum occurs for a perpendicular push: $rF =$ **{tmax:sig3} N·m**.

drills.title: Mass hanging from a heavy pulley
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block hangs from a light rope wrapped around a {M} kg solid cylinder of radius {R} m that turns freely on a frictionless axle. The block is released. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the block's acceleration (m/s²), the rope tension (N) and the cylinder's angular acceleration (rad/s²), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Block: $mg - T = ma$. Cylinder: $TR = \tfrac12MR^2\alpha$ with $\alpha = a/R$, so $T = \tfrac12Ma$.

$a = \dfrac{mg}{m + \tfrac12M} = \dfrac{{m}(9.8)}{{m} + {M}/2} =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = \tfrac12({M})({a:sig3}) =$ **{T:sig3} N**; $\alpha = a/R =$ **{alpha:sig3} rad/s²**.

drills.title: Rolling down a ramp
drills.prompt: A {shape} rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp, dropping a height of {h} m. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its speed at the bottom in m/s, to 3 significant figures. (For comparison, a frictionless sliding block would reach {vs:num2} m/s.)
drills.solution:
With $I = cMR^2$ and $\omega = v/R$: $Mgh = \tfrac12Mv^2 + \tfrac12cMv^2 = \tfrac12(1 + c)Mv^2$, and for a {shape} $c = {shape:num4}$.

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1 + c}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2(9.8)({h})}{1 + {shape:num4}}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Conservation of angular momentum
drills.prompt: A skater spins at {f} rev/s with moment of inertia {I1} kg·m². She pulls in her arms, reducing her moment of inertia to {pct}% of its original value. Find her new spin rate (rev/s) and her new rotational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
No external torque: $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$, so $f_2 = f_1\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{{f}}{{pct}/100} =$ **{f2:sig3} rev/s**.

New $I_2 = {I2:dp3}$ kg·m² and $\omega_2 = 2\pi f_2$; $K_2 = \tfrac12I_2\omega_2^2 =$ **{K2:sig3} J** (up from {K1:num1} J; her muscles did the work).

drills.title: Balancing a seesaw
drills.prompt: A uniform seesaw is pivoted at its center. A {m1} kg person sits {d1} m from the pivot. How far from the pivot, on the other side, must a {m2} kg person sit to balance it? Give meters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about the pivot must cancel (the seesaw's weight and the pivot force act at the pivot): ${m1}g({d1}) = {m2}g\,x$.

$x = \dfrac{{m1}({d1})}{{m2}} =$ **{d2:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Beam on two supports
drills.prompt: A uniform {L} m beam of mass {mb} kg rests on supports at its ends A and B. A {m} kg crate sits {x:num2} m from end A. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the upward force from each support, in newtons to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about A: $F_B({L}) = {mb}(9.8)({L}/2) + {m}(9.8)({x:num2})$, so $F_B =$ **{FB:sig3} N**.

Vertical forces: $F_A = ({mb} + {m})(9.8) - F_B =$ **{FA:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Gravitational force and surface gravity
drills.prompt: A planet has mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², find the acceleration due to gravity at its surface (m/s²) and the weight there of a {m} kg probe (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2} = \dfrac{(6.67\times10^{-11})({Mm}\times10^{{Me}})}{({Rm}\times10^{6})^2} =$ **{gs:sig3} m/s²**.

Weight $= mg = {m}({gs:sig3}) =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Circular orbit speed and period
drills.prompt: A satellite is in a circular orbit {h} km above Earth's surface. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², $M_E = 5.97\times10^{24}$ kg and $R_E = 6.37\times10^{6}$ m, find its orbital speed (m/s) and period (minutes), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Orbit radius from Earth's center: $r = R_E + h = {r:texsci}$ m.

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM_E}{\,r}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{\,v} =$ **{T:sig3} min**.

drills.title: Escape speed
drills.prompt: Find the escape speed (km/s) from the surface of a planet with mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m, and the speed of a circular orbit just above its surface. Use $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg² and give both speeds in km/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Total energy zero: $\tfrac12mv^2 = \dfrac{GMm}{\,R}$, so $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{\,R}} =$ **{ve:sig3} km/s**.

Low orbit: $v = \sqrt{GM/R} = v_{\text{esc}}/\sqrt2 =$ **{vo:sig3} km/s**.

drills.title: Stress, strain and stretch of a wire
drills.prompt: A wire of {mat}, {L} m long and {d} mm in diameter, hangs vertically and supports a {load} kg mass. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the stress in the wire (Pa), the strain, and how much the wire stretches (mm), each to 3 significant figures (type powers of ten like 3.18e-4).
drills.solution:
Force $F = mg = {load}(9.8) = {F:sig4}$ N; area $A = \pi d^2/4 = \pi({d}\times10^{-3})^2/4 = {A:texsci}$ m².

Stress $= F/A = \mathbf{{sig:texsci}}$ Pa. Strain $= \text{stress}/Y = \mathbf{{eps:texsci}}$.

Stretch $\Delta L = \text{strain} \times L = ({eps:texsci})({L}\text{ m}) =$ **{dL:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Period and frequency of a mass on a spring
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block on a frictionless surface is attached to a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m. Find the period (s) and the frequency (Hz) of its oscillation, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m} = \sqrt{{k:dp0}/{m}} = {w:num2}$ rad/s.

$T = 2\pi/\omega = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k} =$ **{T:sig3} s**, and $f = 1/T =$ **{f:sig3} Hz**.

drills.title: Simple pendulum
drills.prompt: A simple pendulum {L} m long swings with small amplitude on {planet}. Find its period in seconds, to 3 significant figures. (Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² on Earth, 1.62 m/s² on the Moon, 3.71 m/s² on Mars.)
drills.solution: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g} = 2\pi\sqrt{{L}/{planet:num2}} =$ **{T:sig3} s**. The bob's mass doesn't matter.

drills.title: Maximum speed and acceleration in SHM
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m) oscillates with amplitude {Acm} cm. Find its maximum speed, its maximum acceleration, and its speed when it is {x:num4} m from equilibrium. Use m/s and m/s², to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m} = {w:num4}$ rad/s.

$v_{\max} = A\omega = ({A})({w:num4}) =$ **{vmax:sig3} m/s**; $a_{\max} = A\omega^2 =$ **{amax:sig3} m/s²**.

From energy, $v = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2} = {w:num4}\sqrt{{A}^2 - {x:num4}^2} =$ **{vx:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Wave speed, frequency and wavelength
drills.prompt: A {f} Hz tone travels as {kind} (speed {kind:int} m/s). Find its wavelength (m) and its period (s), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\lambda = v/f = {kind:dp0}/{f:dp0} =$ **{lam:sig3} m**.

$T = 1/f = 1/{f:dp0} = \mathbf{{T:texsci}}$ s.

drills.title: Harmonics of a stretched string
drills.prompt: A string {L} m long with mass {mg} g is fixed at both ends under {F} N of tension. Find the wave speed, the fundamental frequency and the frequency of harmonic $n = {n}$, to 3 significant figures (m/s and Hz).

drills.title: Intensity and decibels
drills.prompt: A small speaker radiates {P} W of sound equally in all directions. At {r} m away, find the intensity (W/m², to 3 significant figures) and the sound intensity level (dB, to 1 decimal place). Use $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m².
drills.solution:
$I = \dfrac{\,P}{4\pi r^2} = \dfrac{{P}}{4\pi({r})^2} = \mathbf{{I:texsci}}$ W/m².

$\beta = 10\log_{10}\dfrac{\,I}{I_0} =$ **{B:num1} dB**.

drills.title: Doppler shift from a moving source
drills.prompt: A siren emits {f} Hz and moves at {vs} m/s past a stationary listener. Using $v = 343$ m/s, find the frequency heard as it approaches and as it recedes, in Hz to 4 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Approaching source: $f' = f\dfrac{v}{v - v_s} = {f:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{343}{343 - {vs}} =$ **{fa:sig4} Hz**.

Receding: $f' = {f:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{343}{343 + {vs}} =$ **{fr:sig4} Hz**.

drills.title: Resonances of an air column
drills.prompt: A pipe {L} m long is {pipe}. Using $v = 343$ m/s, find its fundamental frequency and the next higher resonant frequency, in Hz to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Open at both ends: $f_n = nv/(2L)$, all $n$. Closed at one end: $f_n = nv/(4L)$, odd $n$ only. This pipe is {pipe}.

$f_1 =$ **{f1:sig3} Hz**, and the next resonance is **{f2:sig3} Hz** ($2f_1$ for an open pipe, $3f_1$ for a closed one).

drills.title: Beats
drills.prompt: Two tuning forks of {f1} Hz and {f2} Hz are struck together. Find the beat frequency and the frequency of the tone you hear throbbing, in Hz (the tone to 1 decimal place).
drills.solution:
$f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2| = |{f1} - {f2}| =$ **{fb} Hz**.

The tone heard is the average frequency, $\tfrac12({f1} + {f2}) =$ **{favg:num1} Hz**, getting louder and softer {fb} times per second.

drills.title: Decay of a damped oscillator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m) is damped by a force $-bv$ with $b = {b}$ kg/s. It starts oscillating with amplitude {A0} cm. Find its quality factor $Q$, the time for the amplitude to fall to half (s), and the amplitude after {tt} s (cm), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$Q = \dfrac{\sqrt{mk}}{\,b} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{m}({k:dp0})}}{{b}} =$ **{Q:sig3}**, so the damping is light and the mass oscillates.

The amplitude decays as $e^{-\gamma t}$ with $\gamma = b/2m = {b}/(2 \times {m}) = {gam:sig4}$ s⁻¹. It halves when $e^{-\gamma t} = \tfrac12$: $t = \ln 2/\gamma =$ **{th:sig3} s**.

After {tt} s: $A = {A0}\,e^{-({gam:sig4})({tt})} =$ **{At:sig3} cm**.

drills.title: Critical damping and the damped frequency
drills.prompt: A mass of {m} kg hangs on a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m. Find the damping constant that would make it critically damped (kg/s). If the actual damping constant is $b = {b}$ kg/s, find the angular frequency at which it oscillates (rad/s). Give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Critical damping means $\gamma = \omega_0$, i.e. $b_c = 2\sqrt{mk} = 2\sqrt{{m}({k:dp0})} =$ **{bc:sig3} kg/s**.

The actual $b = {b}$ kg/s is smaller, so the motion is underdamped. $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {w0:sig4}$ rad/s and $\gamma = b/2m = {gam:sig4}$ s⁻¹, so $\omega' = \sqrt{\omega_0^2 - \gamma^2} =$ **{wd:sig3} rad/s**, noticeably below $\omega_0$.

drills.title: Steady-state amplitude of a driven oscillator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m, damping constant $b = {b}$ kg/s) is driven by a force $F_0\cos\omega t$ with $F_0 = {F0}$ N. Find the steady-state amplitude when $\omega = {w}$ rad/s, and when it is driven at its natural frequency. Give both in cm to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {w0:sig4}$ rad/s and $2\gamma = b/m = {g2:sig4}$ s⁻¹.

$A = \dfrac{F_0/m}{\sqrt{(\omega_0^2 - \omega^2)^2 + (2\gamma\omega)^2}}$ with $\omega = {w}$ rad/s gives **{A:sig3} cm**.

At $\omega_0$ only damping limits it: $A = \dfrac{F_0}{b\,\omega_0} = \dfrac{{F0}}{{b}({w0:sig4})} =$ **{Ar:sig3} cm** (that is $Q = {Q:sig3}$ times the static stretch $F_0/k$).

drills.title: Power carried by a wave on a string
drills.prompt: A string with linear mass density {mug} g/m is under {F} N of tension. A sinusoidal wave of frequency {f} Hz and amplitude {Amm} mm travels along it. Find the wave speed (m/s) and the average power the wave carries (W), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\mu = {mu:dp3}$ kg/m, so $v = \sqrt{F_T/\mu} = \sqrt{{F}/{mu:dp3}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$\omega = 2\pi({f}) = {w:sig4}$ rad/s and $A = {A:dp4}$ m, so $P_{\text{avg}} = \tfrac12\mu A^2\omega^2v = \tfrac12({mu:dp3})({A:dp4})^2({w:sig4})^2({v:sig4}) =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Pressure at depth
drills.prompt: Find the gauge pressure and the absolute pressure {h} m below the surface of {fluid}. Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² and $P_{\text{atm}} = 1.013\times10^5$ Pa, and give both in pascals to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Gauge: $\rho gh = ({fluid:dp0})(9.8)({h}) = \mathbf{{Pg:texsci}}$ Pa.

Absolute: $P_{\text{atm}} + \rho gh = \mathbf{{Pabs:texsci}}$ Pa, about {natm:num2} atm.

drills.title: Apparent weight and floating fraction
drills.prompt: An object of density {rho:dp0} kg/m³ and volume {Vc:dp0} cm³ is held completely under water (density 1000 kg/m³). Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the buoyant force and its apparent weight (weight minus buoyant force; a negative value means it would float up if released), both in newtons to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$V = {Vc:dp0}\text{ cm}^3 = {V:texsci}$ m³. $F_B = \rho_{\text{water}}Vg = 1000({V:texsci})(9.8) =$ **{FB:sig3} N**.

Weight $= \rho Vg = {W:num2}$ N, so weight minus buoyancy $=$ **{app:sig3} N**. A positive value is the force you must hold it up with; a negative value means it is less dense than water and you must push it down.

drills.title: Hydraulic lift
drills.prompt: A hydraulic lift has pistons of diameter {d1} cm and {d2} cm. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², what force on the small piston supports a {m} kg car on the large one, and how far must the small piston move in total to raise the car {h} m? Give the force in newtons and the distance in meters, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Area ratio $= (d_2/d_1)^2 = ({d2}/{d1})^2 = {ratio:sig4}$.

Pascal: $F_1 = \dfrac{mg}{A_2/A_1} = \dfrac{{m:dp0}(9.8)}{{ratio:sig4}} =$ **{F1:sig3} N**.

Equal volumes: $d_1 = {h}({ratio:sig4}) =$ **{s1:sig3} m** (many pump strokes).

drills.title: Continuity equation
drills.prompt: Water flows at {v1} m/s through a pipe of diameter {D1} cm that narrows to {D2} cm. Find the speed in the narrow section (m/s) and the flow rate in liters per second, to 3 significant figures.

drills.title: Pressure in a narrowing horizontal pipe
drills.prompt: Water flows through a horizontal pipe. Where the pressure is {P1k} kPa the speed is {v1} m/s. At a narrower section the speed is {v2} m/s. What is the pressure there, in kPa to 3 significant figures? (Water density 1000 kg/m³.)
drills.solution:
Same height, so $P_1 + \tfrac12\rho v_1^2 = P_2 + \tfrac12\rho v_2^2$:

$P_2 = {P1k}\times10^3 + \tfrac12(1000)({v1}^2 - {v2}^2) = {P2:int}$ Pa $=$ **{P2k:sig3} kPa**. Faster flow, lower pressure.

drills.title: Draining tank (Torricelli)
drills.prompt: A large open tank has a hole of area {a} cm² located {h} m below the water surface. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the speed of the emerging water (m/s) and the initial flow rate in L/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torricelli: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({h})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$Q = Av = ({a}\times10^{-4})({v:num2})$ m³/s $=$ **{Q:sig3} L/s**.

drills.title: Final temperature of a mixture
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg block of {metal} ($c = {metal:dp0}$ J/(kg·K)) at {T1}°C is dropped into {m2} kg of water ($c = 4186$ J/(kg·K)) at {T2}°C in an insulated cup. Ignoring the cup, find the final temperature in °C, to the nearest 0.1°C.

drills.title: Heat to melt and warm ice
drills.prompt: How much heat is needed to turn {m} kg of ice at {Ti}°C into water at {Tf}°C? Use $c_{\text{ice}} = 2100$ J/(kg·K), $L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg and $c_{\text{water}} = 4186$ J/(kg·K), and give the answer in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Warm the ice to 0°C: ${m}(2100)(0 - ({Ti})) = {Q1:dp0}$ J.

Melt it: ${m}(3.34\times10^5) = {Q2:dp0}$ J.

Warm the water: ${m}(4186)({Tf}) = {Q3:dp0}$ J.

Total: $Q = \mathbf{{Q:texsci}}$ J.

drills.title: Thermal expansion
drills.prompt: A {L} m long piece of {mat} warms from {T1}°C to {T2}°C. By how many millimeters does it lengthen? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T = ({mat}\times10^{-6})({L})({T2} - ({T1})) =$ **{dL:sig3} mm**. (A Celsius difference equals a kelvin difference.)

drills.title: Heat conduction through a wall
drills.prompt: A {A} m² panel of {k} is {Lcm} cm thick. The temperature difference across it is {dT} K. Find the rate of heat conduction (W) and the heat lost in one hour (kJ), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{kA\Delta T}{L} = \dfrac{({k:num2})({A})({dT})}{{Lcm}/100} =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

In 3600 s: **{E:sig3} kJ**.

drills.title: Ideal gas law
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas at {TC}°C occupies {VL} L. What is its pressure, in pascals to 3 significant figures? ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
Convert: $T = {TC} + 273.15 = {T:num2}$ K, $V = {VL}\times10^{-3}$ m³.

$P = \dfrac{nRT}{V} = \dfrac{({n})(8.314)({T:num2})}{{VL}\times10^{-3}} = \mathbf{{P:texsci}}$ Pa.

drills.title: Combined gas law
drills.prompt: A gas occupies {V1} L at {P1} atm and {T1} K. What volume does it occupy at {P2} atm and {T2} K? Give liters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$, so $V_2 = V_1\cdot\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\cdot\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = {V1}\cdot\dfrac{{P1}}{{P2}}\cdot\dfrac{{T2}}{{T1}} =$ **{V2:sig3} L**.

drills.title: RMS speed and average kinetic energy
drills.prompt: Find the rms speed of {gas} molecules at {T} K (m/s) and their average translational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K), $k_B = 1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K)
drills.solution:
$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3(8.314)({T:dp0})}{{gas:sig3}}} =$ **{v:int} m/s** ($M$ in kg/mol).

$\overline K = \tfrac32k_BT = \mathbf{{K:texsci}}$ J (the same for every gas at this temperature).

drills.title: First law of thermodynamics
drills.prompt: During a process a gas absorbs {Q} J of heat (negative means it releases heat) and does {W} J of work on its surroundings (negative means work is done on it). Find the change in its internal energy, in joules.
drills.solution: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W = ({Q}) - ({W}) =$ **{dU} J**, with $Q$ into the gas and $W$ done by the gas.

drills.title: Constant-pressure process for a monatomic gas
drills.prompt: {n} mol of a monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure, raising its temperature by {dT} K. Find the work done by the gas, the change in internal energy, and the heat added, in joules to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
$W = P\Delta V = nR\Delta T = ({n})(8.314)({dT}) =$ **{W:sig3} J**.

$\Delta E_{\text{int}} = \tfrac32nR\Delta T =$ **{dU:sig3} J**.

$Q = \Delta E_{\text{int}} + W = \tfrac52nR\Delta T =$ **{Q:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Isothermal expansion
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally at {T} K until its volume is {r} times larger. How much work does it do, and how much heat does it absorb? Give joules to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
$W = \displaystyle\int P\,dV = nRT\ln\frac{V_f}{V_i} = ({n})(8.314)({T})\ln {r} =$ **{W:sig3} J**.

Isothermal: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = 0$, so $Q = W =$ **{W:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Carnot efficiency and heat rejected
drills.prompt: An ideal (Carnot) engine runs between a hot reservoir at {TH}°C and a cold one at {TC}°C. Find its efficiency (as a decimal) and, if it absorbs {QH} J per cycle, the work output and the heat rejected per cycle, in joules. Give all three to 3 significant figures, and convert with $T = T_C + 273$.
drills.solution:
In kelvins, $T_H = {TH} + 273$ and $T_C = {TC} + 273$. $e = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H} =$ **{e:sig3}**.

$W = eQ_H =$ **{W:sig3} J**; $Q_C = Q_H - W =$ **{QC:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Engine efficiency from work and exhaust heat
drills.prompt: An engine does {W} J of work per cycle and exhausts {QC} J of heat. How much heat does it absorb per cycle (J), and what is its efficiency (as a decimal to 3 significant figures)?
drills.solution:
First law over a cycle: $Q_H = W + Q_C = {W:dp0} + {QC:dp0} =$ **{QH:dp0} J**.

$e = W/Q_H =$ **{e:sig3}**.

drills.title: Entropy change of melting and of heating
drills.prompt: {m} kg of ice at 0°C melts, and the water is then warmed to {T2}°C. Find the entropy change for (a) the melting and (b) the warming, in J/K to 3 significant figures. ($L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg, $c = 4186$ J/(kg·K), 0°C = 273.15 K)
drills.solution:
(a) Constant temperature: $\Delta S = \dfrac{mL_f}{T} = \dfrac{{m}(3.34\times10^5)}{273.15} =$ **{S1:sig3} J/K**.

(b) $\Delta S = \displaystyle\int\frac{mc\,dT}{T} = mc\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} = {m}(4186)\ln\frac{{T2} + 273.15}{273.15} =$ **{S2:sig3} J/K**.

drills.title: Atwood machine with a massive pulley (Lagrangian)
drills.prompt: Blocks of {m1:dp1} kg and {m2:dp1} kg hang on either side of a light string over a pulley that is a uniform disk of mass {mp:dp1} kg. The string doesn't slip. Using $L = T - U$ with the heavier block's drop $x$ as the coordinate and $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the acceleration of the blocks (m/s²) and the tension in the string on the heavier block's side (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The pulley turns at $\omega = \dot x/R$, so $T = \tfrac12\left(m_1 + m_2 + \tfrac12M\right)\dot x^2$ with $m_1 + m_2 + \tfrac12M = {meff:sig3}$ kg, and $U = -(m_1 - m_2)gx$.

Euler–Lagrange: $({meff:sig3})\ddot x = ({m1:dp1} - {m2:dp1})(9.8)$, so $a =$ **{acc:sig3} m/s²**.

The tension doesn't appear in the Lagrangian; get it from Newton's law for the heavier block: tension $= m_1(g - a) = {m1:dp1}(9.8 - {acc:sig3}) =$ **{T1:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Swinging rod from its Lagrangian
drills.prompt: A uniform rod of length {len:num2} m swings about a pivot at one end. Its Lagrangian is $L = \tfrac16m\ell^2\dot\theta^2 + \tfrac12mg\ell\cos\theta$. For small swings, find the angular frequency (rad/s) and the period (s), to 3 significant figures, using $g = 9.8$ m/s².
drills.solution:
Euler–Lagrange: $\tfrac13m\ell^2\ddot\theta = -\tfrac12mg\ell\sin\theta \approx -\tfrac12mg\ell\,\theta$, so $\ddot\theta = -\dfrac{3g}{2\ell}\theta$.

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3(9.8)}{2({len:num2})}} =$ **{w:sig3} rad/s**; period $= 2\pi/\omega =$ **{P:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Puck on a string through a hole
drills.prompt: A {m:num2} kg puck on a frictionless table is tied to a string through a hole at the center. It circles at radius {ra:num2} m with angular speed {w1:dp1} rad/s, and the string is slowly pulled until the radius is {rb:num2} m. Find the new angular speed (rad/s) and the work done by the person pulling the string (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The force is central, so the angle is a cyclic coordinate and $mr^2\dot\varphi$ is conserved: $\omega_2 = {w1:dp1}\left(\dfrac{{ra:num2}}{{rb:num2}}\right)^2 =$ **{w2:sig3} rad/s**.

$T_1 = \tfrac12m r_1^2\omega_1^2 = {K1:sig3}$ J and $T_2 = \tfrac12m r_2^2\omega_2^2 = {K2:sig3}$ J. The work done by the pull is the gain: **{W:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Oscillator ellipse in phase space
drills.prompt: A mass of {m:num2} kg on a spring with $k = {k}$ N/m has total energy {E:dp1} J. Its phase-space path is an ellipse. Find the semi-axes: the amplitude $x_{\max}$ (m) and the largest momentum $p_{\max}$ (kg·m/s), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$H = \dfrac{p^2}{2m} + \tfrac12kx^2 = E$.

At $p = 0$: $x_{\max} = \sqrt{2E/k} = \sqrt{2({E:dp1})/{k}} =$ **{xm:sig3} m**.

At $x = 0$: $p_{\max} = \sqrt{2mE} = \sqrt{2({m:num2})({E:dp1})} =$ **{pm:sig3} kg·m/s**.

drills.title: Elliptical Earth orbit from perigee and apogee
drills.prompt: A satellite's perigee is {hp} km and its apogee {ha} km above Earth's surface. Using $R_E = 6370$ km and $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find the semimajor axis (km), the eccentricity, and the period (minutes), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Distances from Earth's center: $r_p = {rp:sig5}$ km and $r_a = {rap:sig5}$ km.

$a = \tfrac12(r_p + r_a) =$ **{sma:sig3} km**; $e = \dfrac{r_a - r_p}{r_a + r_p} =$ **{ecc:sig3}**.

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{a^3/GM}$ with $a$ in meters: **{T:sig3} min**.

drills.title: Speeds at perigee and apogee (vis-viva)
drills.prompt: An Earth satellite's orbit ranges from {rp} km to {rap} km from Earth's center. Using $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find its speed at perigee and at apogee in km/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$a = \tfrac12({rp:sig5} + {rap:sig5}) = {sma:sig5}$ km. Vis-viva, $v^2 = GM\left(\dfrac{2}{\,r} - \dfrac{1}{\,a}\right)$, with distances in meters:

Perigee: **{vp:sig3} km/s**. Apogee: **{va:sig3} km/s**.

Check: $r_pv_p = r_av_a$ (angular momentum), and both products are about {hv:sig3} km²/s.

drills.title: Orbit from position and speed
drills.prompt: A spacecraft is {r} km from Earth's center, moving at {v:dp1} km/s perpendicular to the line to the center. Using $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find its specific orbital energy (MJ/kg), the semimajor axis of its orbit (km), and its farthest distance from Earth's center (km), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\varepsilon = \dfrac{v^2}{2} - \dfrac{GM}{\,r} =$ **{epsm:sig3} MJ/kg**: negative, so the orbit is an ellipse.

$a = -\dfrac{GM}{2\varepsilon} =$ **{sma:sig3} km**.

The velocity is perpendicular to $\vec r$, so this is a turning point; the speed is above the circular speed ({vc:sig3} km/s), so it is perigee. Apogee: $r_a = 2a - r_p =$ **{rother:sig3} km**.

drills.title: Hohmann transfer between Earth orbits
drills.prompt: A satellite moves by a Hohmann transfer from a circular orbit {h1} km above Earth's surface to one {h2} km up. Using $R_E = 6370$ km and $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find the two burns (km/s) and the coasting time (hours), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Radii: $r_1 = {r1:texsci}$ m, $r_2 = {r2:texsci}$ m; transfer orbit $a_t = {at:texsci}$ m.

Burn 1: transfer periapsis speed minus circular speed at $r_1$: **{dv1:sig3} km/s**.

Burn 2: circular speed at $r_2$ minus transfer apoapsis speed: **{dv2:sig3} km/s** (total {tot:sig3} km/s).

Coast: half the transfer period, $\pi\sqrt{a_t^3/GM} =$ **{hrs:sig3} h**.

drills.title: Hohmann transfer to an outer planet
drills.prompt: Model Earth's orbit (1.00 AU) and that of {R} as circles in one plane. For a Hohmann transfer from Earth, find the trip time in days (1 yr = 365.25 days) and how many degrees the target must be ahead of Earth at launch, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
In AU and years, $T^2 = a^3$. The transfer orbit has $a_t = \tfrac12(1 + {Rn:sig3}) = {at:sig3}$ AU, and the trip is half its period: $t = \tfrac12({at:sig3})^{3/2} = {yrs:sig3}$ yr $=$ **{days:sig3} days**.

The target's period is ${Rn:sig3}^{3/2} = {TP:sig3}$ yr, so during the trip it moves $360^\circ \times {yrs:sig3}/{TP:sig3}$. The spacecraft covers $180^\circ$, so the target must lead by **{lead:sig3}°**.

drills.title: Departure burn from a parking orbit
drills.prompt: A spacecraft in a circular orbit {h} km above Earth's surface must leave Earth with a hyperbolic excess speed of {vinf:dp1} km/s. Using $R_E = 6370$ km and $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find the speed it needs just after a single forward burn and the size of that burn, both in km/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$r = {r:texsci}$ m. Circular speed $\sqrt{GM/r} = {vc:sig3}$ km/s; escape speed $\sqrt{2GM/r} = {ve:sig3}$ km/s.

Energy: $v = \sqrt{v_\infty^2 + v_{\text{esc}}^2} = \sqrt{{vinf:dp1}^2 + {ve:sig3}^2} =$ **{vb:sig3} km/s**.

Burn: $v - v_{\text{circ}} =$ **{dv:sig3} km/s**. (Escaping first and then adding {vinf:dp1} km/s far away would cost {two:sig3} km/s: the Oberth effect.)

drills.title: Mean, standard deviation and standard error
drills.prompt: Five timings of the same event are {r1:num2}, {r2:num2}, {r3:num2}, {r4:num2} and {r5:num2} s. Find the mean (exact, to 3 decimal places), the sample standard deviation and the standard error of the mean (each to 2 significant figures).
drills.solution:
Mean: $\bar t = \dfrac{ {r1:num2} + {r2:num2} + {r3:num2} + {r4:num2} + {r5:num2} }{5} =$ **{m:dp3} s**.

Standard deviation (divide by $n - 1 = 4$): $s = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (t_i - \bar t)^2}{4}} =$ **{sd:sig2} s**.

Standard error: $\delta\bar t = \dfrac{s}{\sqrt5} = \dfrac{ {sd:sig3} }{2.236} =$ **{se:sig2} s**.

drills.title: g from a pendulum, with uncertainty
drills.prompt: A pendulum has length $L = {L:dp3} \pm {dL:dp3}$ m and period $T = {T:dp3} \pm {dT:dp3}$ s. Find $g = 4\pi^2 L/T^2$ (3 significant figures) and its uncertainty $\delta g$, combining relative uncertainties in quadrature (2 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$g = \dfrac{4\pi^2({L:dp3})}{({T:dp3})^2} =$ **{grav:sig3} m/s²**.

Relative uncertainties: $\dfrac{\delta L}{L} = \dfrac{ {dL:dp3} }{ {L:dp3} } = {rL:sig3}$; $T$ is squared, so it contributes $2\dfrac{\delta T}{T} = {rT:sig3}$.

$\dfrac{\delta g}{g} = \sqrt{({rL:sig3})^2 + ({rT:sig3})^2} = {rel:sig3}$, so $\delta g = {rel:sig3} \times {grav:sig3} =$ **{dg:sig2} m/s²**.

drills.title: Volume of a sphere, with uncertainty
drills.prompt: A ball bearing has diameter $d = {dia:num2} \pm {dd:num2}$ cm. Find its volume $V = \pi d^3/6$ in cm³ (3 significant figures) and the uncertainty $\delta V$ (2 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$V = \dfrac{\pi({dia:num2})^3}{6} =$ **{V:sig3} cm³**.

$d$ is cubed, so the relative uncertainty triples: $\dfrac{\delta V}{V} = 3\cdot\dfrac{ {dd:num2} }{ {dia:num2} } = {rel:sig3}$.

$\delta V = {rel:sig3} \times {V:sig3} =$ **{dV:sig2} cm³**.

drills.title: Scalar projection and perpendicular part
drills.prompt: For $\vec A = {a1:coef}\hat\imath {a2:signedcoef}\hat\jmath {a3:signedcoef}\hat k$ and $\vec B = {b1:coef}\hat\imath {b2:signedcoef}\hat\jmath {b3:signedcoef}\hat k$, find the scalar projection of $\vec A$ onto $\vec B$ (with its sign) and the magnitude of the part of $\vec A$ perpendicular to $\vec B$, each to 3 significant figures. Keep exact values until the end (don't reuse the rounded projection).
drills.solution:
$\vec A\cdot\vec B = ({a1})({b1}) + ({a2})({b2}) + ({a3})({b3}) = {dot}$ and $|\vec B| = {B:sig4}$, so $\vec A\cdot\hat B = \dfrac{ {dot} }{ {B:sig4} } =$ **{sp:sig3}**.

$|\vec A|^2 = ({a1})^2 + ({a2})^2 + ({a3})^2 = {A2}$ and $|\vec B|^2 = {B2}$. The two parts are perpendicular, so $|\vec A_\perp| = \sqrt{|\vec A|^2 - (\vec A\cdot\hat B)^2} = \sqrt{ {A2} - \dfrac{ ({dot})^2 }{ {B2} } } =$ **{perp:sig3}**.

drills.title: Components in rotated axes
drills.prompt: A force of {F} N points at {th}° counterclockwise from the $+x$ axis. New axes $x'$ and $y'$ are the old ones rotated {ph}° counterclockwise. Find $F_{x'}$ and $F_{y'}$ (with signs), each to 3 significant figures.

figure.caption: F = {F} N at {th}°; dashed lines are the rotated axes

drills.solution:
Old components: $F_x = {F}\cos{th}^\circ = {Fx:sig4}$ N and $F_y = {F}\sin{th}^\circ = {Fy:sig4}$ N.

$F_{x'} = F_x\cos{ph}^\circ + F_y\sin{ph}^\circ =$ **{Fxp:sig3} N**

$F_{y'} = -F_x\sin{ph}^\circ + F_y\cos{ph}^\circ =$ **{Fyp:sig3} N**

Shortcut: the force makes angle ${th}^\circ - {ph}^\circ$ with the new $x'$ axis, so $F_{x'} = F\cos({th}^\circ - {ph}^\circ)$ and $F_{y'} = F\sin({th}^\circ - {ph}^\circ)$.

drills.title: Scalar triple product and volume
drills.prompt: For $\vec A = {a1:coef}\hat\imath {a2:signedcoef}\hat\jmath {a3:signedcoef}\hat k$, $\vec B = {b1:coef}\hat\imath {b2:signedcoef}\hat\jmath {b3:signedcoef}\hat k$ and $\vec C = {c1:coef}\hat\imath {c2:signedcoef}\hat\jmath {c3:signedcoef}\hat k$ (in meters), find the scalar triple product $\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec C)$ and the volume of the parallelepiped they span (exact).
drills.solution:
$\vec B\times\vec C = ({k1})\hat\imath + ({k2})\hat\jmath + ({k3})\hat k$.

$\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec C) = ({a1})({k1}) + ({a2})({k2}) + ({a3})({k3}) =$ **{t}**

The volume is the absolute value: **{vol} m³**.

drills.title: Two launch angles that hit a target
drills.prompt: A ball is launched at {v0} m/s toward a target {x} m away horizontally and {y} m above the launch point. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s² and no air resistance, find both launch angles above horizontal that hit the target, each to the nearest 0.1°.
drills.solution:
With $u = \tan\theta$ and $k = \dfrac{gx^2}{2v_0^2} = \dfrac{9.8({x})^2}{2({v0})^2} = {k:sig4}$ m, the target condition is $ku^2 - xu + (y + k) = 0$:

$${k:sig4}\,u^2 - {x}\,u + {c:sig4} = 0.$$

Discriminant: ${x}^2 - 4({k:sig4})({c:sig4}) = {disc:sig4}$, positive, so two angles work.

$u = \dfrac{{x} \pm \sqrt{{disc:sig4}}}{2({k:sig4})} = {u1:sig4}$ or ${u2:sig4}$.

So $\theta =$ **{lo:num1}°** (low shot) and **{hi:num1}°** (lob).

drills.title: Minimum launch speed to reach a point
drills.prompt: A target is {x} m away horizontally and {y} m above the launch point (negative means below). Using $g = 9.8$ m/s² and no air resistance, find the smallest launch speed that can reach it (3 significant figures) and the launch angle above horizontal that it requires (nearest 0.1°).
drills.solution:
Straight-line distance: $d = \sqrt{{x}^2 + ({y})^2} = {d:sig4}$ m.

$v_{0,\min}^2 = g(y + d) = 9.8({y} + {d:sig4})$, so $v_{0,\min} =$ **{vmin:sig3} m/s**.

Angle: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{y + d}{\,x} = \dfrac{{y} + {d:sig4}}{{x}}$, so $\theta =$ **{th:num1}°**. (Check: the line to the target is at $\alpha = {al:num1}°$, and $45° + \alpha/2$ gives the same angle.)

drills.title: Range along a slope
drills.prompt: A ball is thrown at {v0} m/s from the bottom of a slope that rises at {al}°. (a) If it is thrown at {th}° above horizontal, how far up the slope (measured along it) does it land? (b) What is the greatest distance up the slope any launch angle can reach at this speed? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s²; give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $L = \dfrac{2v_0^2\cos\theta\sin(\theta - \alpha)}{g\cos^2\alpha} = \dfrac{2({v0})^2\cos {th}°\sin {dth}°}{9.8\cos^2 {al}°} =$ **{L:sig3} m**.

(b) The best angle is $45° + \alpha/2 = {best}°$, and $L_{\max} = \dfrac{v_0^2}{g(1 + \sin\alpha)} = \dfrac{{v0}^2}{9.8(1 + \sin {al}°)} =$ **{Lmax:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Tangential and normal acceleration from r(t)
drills.prompt: A particle moves with $\vec r(t) = ({p:coef}t^2)\,\hat\imath + ({q:coef}t {c:signedcoef}t^3)\,\hat\jmath$ (meters, seconds). At $t = {T}$ s, find its tangential acceleration (negative if it is slowing down), its normal acceleration and the radius of curvature of its path, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\vec v = ({p2}t,\ {q} {c3:signed}t^2)$ and $\vec a = ({p2},\ {c6}t)$. At $t = {T}$ s: $\vec v = ({vx}, {vy})$ m/s, $\vec a = ({ax}, {ay})$ m/s², speed $v = {sp:sig4}$ m/s.

$a_t = \dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec v}{v} = \dfrac{{dot}}{{sp:sig4}} =$ **{at:sig3} m/s²**.

$v_xa_y - v_ya_x = {cr}$, so $a_n = \dfrac{|{cr}|}{{sp:sig4}} =$ **{an:sig3} m/s²**.

$\rho = \dfrac{v^2}{a_n} =$ **{rho:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Radius of curvature of a projectile's path
drills.prompt: A ball is launched at {v0} m/s, {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s² and no air resistance, find the radius of curvature of its path just after launch and at the top of its flight, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
At launch the normal part of $g$ is $a_n = g\cos\theta = 9.8\cos {th}° = {an0:sig4}$ m/s², so $\rho = \dfrac{v_0^2}{a_n} = \dfrac{{v0}^2}{{an0:sig4}} =$ **{rl:sig3} m**.

At the top $v = v_x = {v0}\cos {th}° = {vx:sig4}$ m/s and all of $g$ is normal, so $\rho = \dfrac{v_x^2}{g} =$ **{rt:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Stacked blocks on the verge of slipping
drills.prompt: A block of mass {mt} kg rests on a board of mass {mb} kg, which lies on a frictionless floor. The coefficient of static friction between block and board is {mus}. You pull the board horizontally. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the largest acceleration the pair can have without the block slipping, and the pull that gives it. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Only friction from the board accelerates the block, and it can be at most $\mu_s m_{\text{top}}g$, so the block's largest acceleration is $\mu_s g = {mus}(9.8) =$ **{amax:sig3} m/s²**.

Moving together, the whole $({mt} + {mb})$ kg system has that acceleration: $F = ({mt} + {mb})({amax:sig4}) =$ **{Fmax:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Best angle to drag a crate
drills.prompt: A crate of mass {m} kg is dragged at constant speed across a floor with $\mu_k = {mu}$ by a rope. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the rope angle above horizontal that needs the least force, and that least force. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$F(\theta) = \dfrac{\mu mg}{\cos\theta + \mu\sin\theta}$ is smallest where $\tan\theta = \mu$: $\theta = \tan^{-1}({mu}) =$ **{th:sig3}°**.

Then $F_{\min} = \dfrac{\mu mg}{\sqrt{1 + \mu^2}} = \dfrac{{Fh:sig4}}{\sqrt{1 + {mu}^2}} =$ **{Fmin:sig3} N** (a horizontal pull would need {Fh:sig3} N).

drills.title: Rope wrapped around a post
drills.prompt: A rope is wrapped {turns} around a fixed post, with $\mu_s = {mu}$ between rope and post. You hold one end with {Th} N. Find the ratio of load tension to holding tension when the rope is on the verge of slipping, and the largest load tension you can resist. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Wrap angle in radians: $\theta = 2\pi({turns:num1}) = {wrap:sig4}$ rad. Capstan equation: $T_{\text{load}}/T_{\text{hold}} = e^{\mu\theta} = e^{{mu}({wrap:sig4})} =$ **{ratio:sig3}**.

Largest load: $T_{\text{load}} = {Th}({ratio:sig4}) =$ **{Tl:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Falling with quadratic drag
drills.prompt: A skydiver of mass {m} kg falls from rest with drag coefficient {C} and cross-sectional area {A} m², in air of density 1.2 kg/m³. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s² and quadratic drag, find the terminal speed and the time to reach {p} of it. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$c = \tfrac12 C\rho A = \tfrac12({C})(1.2)({A}) = {c:sig4}$ kg/m, so $v_T = \sqrt{mg/c} = \sqrt{{m}(9.8)/{c:sig4}} =$ **{vT:sig3} m/s**.

With $v = v_T\tanh(gt/v_T)$, the time to reach {p} of $v_T$ is $t = \dfrac{v_T}{g}\tanh^{-1}({p:num2}) = {tau:sig4}\tanh^{-1}({p:num2}) =$ **{t:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Coasting with quadratic drag
drills.prompt: A boat of mass {m} kg, coasting at {v0} m/s, feels water drag $cv^2$ with $c = {c}$ kg/m and no other horizontal force. Find how long it takes to slow to half its speed, and its speed after it has traveled {x} m. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
From $m\,dv/dt = -cv^2$: $v = \dfrac{v_0}{1 + cv_0t/m}$, which halves when $t = \dfrac{\,m}{cv_0} = \dfrac{{m}}{{c}({v0})} =$ **{th:sig3} s**.

Using $dv/dt = v\,dv/dx$: $v = v_0e^{-cx/m} = {v0}\,e^{-{c}({x})/{m}} =$ **{vx:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Pendulum in an accelerating vehicle
drills.prompt: A small mass hangs from a string inside a van that accelerates forward at {acc} m/s². Once it stops swinging, at what angle from vertical does the string hang, and what is the effective gravity in the van? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
In the van's frame, tension, weight and the fictitious force $-mA$ balance: $T\cos\theta = mg$ and $T\sin\theta = mA$, so $\tan\theta = A/g = {acc}/9.8$ and $\theta =$ **{th:sig3}°** (toward the rear).

$g_{\text{eff}} = \sqrt{9.8^2 + {acc}^2} =$ **{geff:sig3} m/s²**.

drills.title: Artificial gravity in a rotating station
drills.prompt: A ring-shaped space station of radius {r} m spins so that people on its outer floor feel an effective gravity of {fr} times $g = 9.8$ m/s². Find the angular speed in rad/s and the spin rate in revolutions per minute. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The centrifugal force $m\omega^2 r$ plays the role of weight: $\omega^2 r = {fr}(9.8) = {geff:sig4}$ m/s², so $\omega = \sqrt{{geff:sig4}/{r}} =$ **{w:sig3} rad/s**.

Spin rate: $\omega\cdot\dfrac{60}{2\pi} =$ **{rpm:sig3} rpm**.

drills.title: Work by a conservative force in the plane
drills.prompt: A force $\vec F = ({a2}xy {b:signed},\; {a:coef}x^2)$ N acts in the $xy$-plane ($x$, $y$ in m). It passes the curl test. Find the work it does on a particle that moves from the origin to $({X}, {Y})$ m along any path. Give the exact value in joules.
drills.solution:
Curl test: $\partial F_y/\partial x = {a2}x = \partial F_x/\partial y$, so a potential exists.

$U = -\int F_x\,dx = -({a:coef}x^2y {b:signedcoef}x) + g(y)$, and $-\partial U/\partial y = {a:coef}x^2 - g'(y)$ must equal $F_y = {a:coef}x^2$, so $g$ is a constant (take 0).

$W = -\Delta U = U(0, 0) - U({X}, {Y}) = 0 - ({U}) =$ **{W} J**.

drills.title: Force from a two-dimensional potential energy
drills.prompt: A particle has potential energy $U(x, y) = {a:coef}x^2 + {b:coef}y^2 {c:signedcoef}xy$ J ($x$, $y$ in m). Find the components of the force on it at $({x0}, {y0})$ m (exact, in N) and the magnitude of the force in N to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\vec F = -\nabla U$: $F_x = -\dfrac{\partial U}{\partial x} = -({a2}x {c:signedcoef}y)$ and $F_y = -\dfrac{\partial U}{\partial y} = -({b2}y {c:signedcoef}x)$.

At $({x0}, {y0})$: $F_x =$ **{Fx} N**, $F_y =$ **{Fy} N**.

Magnitude: $\sqrt{({Fx})^2 + ({Fy})^2} =$ **{Fm:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Rocket rising against gravity
drills.prompt: A rocket of total mass {mt} t (1 t = 1000 kg) rises vertically. Propellant making up {pct}% of the mass burns at a steady {R:dp0} kg/s, with exhaust speed {uex:dp0} m/s relative to the rocket. Ignoring drag and using $g = 9.8$ m/s² throughout, find the thrust (N), the acceleration at liftoff (m/s²) and the speed at burnout (m/s), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Thrust: $uR = ({uex:dp0})({R:dp0}) = {T:texsci}$ N, that is **{T:sig3} N**.

Liftoff: $a = \dfrac{uR}{m_i} - g = \dfrac{{T:texsci}}{{mi:texsci}} - 9.8 =$ **{a0:sig3} m/s²**.

Burn time: $t_b = \dfrac{0.{pct}\times{mi:dp0}\text{ kg}}{{R:dp0}\text{ kg/s}} = {tb:sig3}$ s, and $m_i/m_f = 1/(1 - {pct}/100)$.

Burnout: $v = u\ln\dfrac{m_i}{m_f} - gt_b = {uex:dp0}\ln\dfrac{1}{1 - {pct}/100} - 9.8({tb:sig3}) =$ **{vb:sig3} m/s** (gravity loss {gl:sig3} m/s).

drills.title: Force and power to run a loading conveyor
drills.prompt: Gravel falls straight down onto a horizontal conveyor belt at {R} kg/s. The belt moves at a constant {v} m/s. Find the extra horizontal force the belt must exert (N), the extra power the motor supplies (W), and the rate at which energy becomes heat (W), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The gravel arrives with no horizontal velocity, so its relative velocity is $-v$ and $0 = F - vR$: $F = Rv = {R}({v}) =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

Power: $P = Fv = Rv^2 =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

The gravel gains kinetic energy at $\tfrac12Rv^2$; the other half becomes heat: **{Q:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Force of a water jet on a wall
drills.prompt: A horizontal water jet {dcm} cm in diameter hits a wall head-on at {v} m/s and splashes out sideways along the wall. Taking $\rho = 1000$ kg/m³, find the mass flow rate (kg/s) and the force the jet exerts on the wall (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Area: $A = \pi({dcm}/200\text{ m})^2 = {A:sig3}$ m².

Mass flow rate: $\rho Av = 1000({A:sig3})({v}) =$ **{mr:sig3} kg/s**.

The wall removes all the forward momentum, so $F = \rho Av^2 = ({mr:sig3})({v}) =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: A one-dimensional collision through the CM frame
drills.prompt: A cart of mass {ma} kg moving at {v1} m/s hits a cart of mass {mb} kg at rest head-on. The coefficient of restitution is {rest}. Find the kinetic energy lost (J, 3 significant figures) and the final velocities of both carts (m/s, 2 decimal places; positive in the original direction of motion).
drills.solution:
$v_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{{ma}({v1})}{{ma} + {mb}} = {vcm:dp3}$ m/s and $\mu = \dfrac{({ma})({mb})}{{ma} + {mb}} = {mu:dp3}$ kg.

Relative kinetic energy: $\tfrac12\mu v_{\text{rel}}^2 = \tfrac12({mu:dp3})({v1})^2 = {Krel:sig3}$ J. Lost: $(1 - {rest}^2)({Krel:sig3}) =$ **{Kl:sig3} J**.

In the CM frame the carts move at ${v1} - {vcm:dp3}$ and $-{vcm:dp3}$ m/s; the collision reverses both and multiplies them by {rest}. Adding $v_{\text{cm}}$ back: $v_{1f} = v_{\text{cm}} - {rest}(v_1 - v_{\text{cm}}) =$ **{v1f:num2} m/s** and $v_{2f} = (1 + {rest})v_{\text{cm}} =$ **{v2f:num2} m/s**.

drills.title: Energy transfer and largest deflection angle
drills.prompt: A particle of mass {ma} u collides elastically with a particle of mass {mb} u at rest. (a) In a head-on collision, what fraction of the projectile's kinetic energy goes to the target? Give a decimal to 3 significant figures. (b) In a glancing collision, what is the largest angle through which the projectile can be deflected? Give degrees to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution:
(a) $\dfrac{4m_1m_2}{(m_1 + m_2)^2} = \dfrac{4({ma})({mb})}{({ma} + {mb})^2} =$ **{fr:sig3}**.

(b) The projectile is heavier, so $\sin\theta_{\max} = m_2/m_1 = {mb}/{ma}$ and $\theta_{\max} =$ **{th:num1}°**.

drills.title: From skidding to rolling
drills.prompt: A {shape} is launched along a level floor at {v0} m/s with no spin. The coefficient of kinetic friction is {mu}. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find how long it slides (s), its speed when it starts rolling without slipping (m/s), and how far it slides (m), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
For a {shape}, $I = cMR^2$ with $c = {shape:num4}$. Friction $\mu_kMg$ slows the center, $v = v_0 - \mu_kgt$, and spins the object up, $R\omega = \mu_kgt/c$.

They match when $t^* = \dfrac{c\,v_0}{(1 + c)\mu_kg} = \dfrac{{shape:num4}({v0})}{(1 + {shape:num4})({mu})(9.8)} =$ **{ts:sig3} s**.

Rolling speed (also from angular momentum about a floor point): $v_f = \dfrac{v_0}{1 + c} =$ **{vf:sig3} m/s**.

Distance: $d = v_0t^* - \tfrac12\mu_kg(t^*)^2 =$ **{dist:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Center of percussion of a rod
drills.prompt: A uniform rod {L} m long is held at a pivot {p:num2} m from its top end and hangs straight down. A ball strikes it horizontally. Find the distance from the pivot to the rod's center of mass, and the distance from the pivot to its center of percussion (where a blow gives no jolt at the pivot), in meters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Center of mass: $d = \tfrac L2 - {p:num2} =$ **{d:sig3} m** below the pivot.

Parallel-axis theorem: $I_P = \tfrac1{12}ML^2 + Md^2$. With no impulse at the pivot, $b = \dfrac{I_P}{Md} = d + \dfrac{L^2}{12d} = {d:sig4} + \dfrac{({L})^2}{12({d:sig4})} =$ **{b:sig3} m** below the pivot ({fromend:sig3} m from the top end).

drills.title: Gyroscope precession
drills.prompt: A gyroscope's rotor is a uniform {M} kg disk of radius {R} m spinning at {rpm} rpm. Its center is {r} m from the pivot and its axle is horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its spin angular momentum (kg·m²/s), the torque of gravity about the pivot (N·m), and the precession rate (rad/s), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$I = \tfrac12MR^2 = {I:texsci}$ kg·m² and $\omega = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w:num2}$ rad/s, so $L = I\omega =$ **{L:sig3} kg·m²/s**.

$\tau = Mgr = {M}(9.8)({r}) =$ **{tau:sig3} N·m**.

$\Omega = \dfrac{\tau}{\,L} =$ **{Om:sig3} rad/s**, one precession every {Tp:sig3} s. (The spin is much faster than the precession, so the gyroscopic approximation holds.)

drills.title: Bearing torque from a crooked rotor
drills.prompt: Two small {m} kg masses sit at the ends of a light rod, each {a} m from its center. The rod is fixed through its center to a shaft but is {tilt}° off perpendicular (so it makes $\beta = {beta}^\circ$ with the shaft). The shaft turns at {w} rad/s in bearings {sep} m apart. Find the sideways component of the angular momentum (kg·m²/s), the torque the bearings must supply (N·m), and the force on each bearing (N), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Each mass has angular momentum $ma(\omega a\sin\beta)$ perpendicular to the rod; the sideways part of the total is $L_\perp = 2ma^2\omega\sin\beta\cos\beta = 2({m})({a})^2({w})\sin {beta}^\circ\cos {beta}^\circ =$ **{Lp:sig3} kg·m²/s**.

It turns with the shaft, so $\tau = \omega L_\perp =$ **{tau:sig3} N·m**.

The bearings supply it as a couple: $F = \tau/{sep} =$ **{F:sig3} N** each, in opposite directions.

drills.title: Gravity inside a uniform planet
drills.prompt: A uniform planet has mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², find the surface gravity (m/s²), the gravitational acceleration {pct}% of the way from the center to the surface (m/s²), and the time (minutes) for an object dropped into a frictionless tunnel through the center to reach the far side, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$g_s = \dfrac{GM}{R^2} =$ **{gs:sig3} m/s²**.

Inside a uniform planet only the mass within $r$ counts, so $g = g_s\dfrac{r}{\,R} = {gs:sig4}({pct}/100) =$ **{gin:sig3} m/s²**.

The tunnel motion is simple harmonic with period $2\pi\sqrt{R/g_s}$; one way is half a period: $\pi\sqrt{R/g_s} =$ **{trip:sig3} min**.

drills.title: Direct pull and tidal acceleration
drills.prompt: A moon of mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg orbits ${Dm}\times10^{8}$ m from Earth's center. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg² and $R_E = 6.37\times10^{6}$ m, find the moon's gravitational acceleration at Earth's center (m/s²), its tidal acceleration at the point of Earth's surface nearest it, using $2GMR_E/D^3$ (m/s²), and that tidal acceleration as a multiple of our Moon's ($1.10\times10^{-6}$ m/s²), each to 3 significant figures (type powers of ten like 3.18e-4).
drills.solution:
Direct pull: $\dfrac{GM}{D^2} = \dfrac{(6.67\times10^{-11})({Mm}\times10^{{Me}})}{({Dm}\times10^{8})^2} = \mathbf{{direct:texsci}}$ m/s².

Tidal: $\dfrac{2GMR_E}{D^3} = \mathbf{{tidal:texsci}}$ m/s², smaller than the direct pull by the factor $2R_E/D$.

Compared with the Moon: $\dfrac{{tidal:texsci}}{1.10\times10^{-6}} =$ **{ratio:sig3}**.

drills.title: Harmonics of a square wave
drills.prompt: A square wave switches between $+{A}$ V and $-{A}$ V with equal halves, and its fundamental frequency is {f} Hz. Find the frequency (Hz) and the amplitude (V) of harmonic number {n}, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
A square wave has only odd harmonics, with amplitudes $b_n = \dfrac{4A}{n\pi}$.

Harmonic {n} has frequency ${n} \times {f} =$ **{fn:int} Hz** and amplitude $\dfrac{4 \times {A}}{{n}\pi} =$ **{bn:sig3} V**.

drills.title: Harmonics of a plucked string
drills.prompt: A string fixed at both ends is pulled aside at a point $1/{p}$ of its length from one end and released. Find (a) the starting amplitude of harmonic {n} as a fraction of the fundamental's amplitude, to 3 significant figures, and (b) the lowest-numbered harmonic that is missing from its sound.
drills.solution:
With $d/L = 1/{p}$, the amplitudes are $B_n \propto \dfrac{\sin(n\pi d/L)}{n^2}$, so

$\dfrac{B_n}{B_1} = \dfrac{\sin({n}\pi/{p})}{{n}^2\sin(\pi/{p})} =$ **{r:sig3}**.

A harmonic is missing when the pluck point is one of its nodes, i.e. when $\sin(n\pi/{p}) = 0$. The first such harmonic is number **{p}**.

drills.title: Normal modes of two coupled masses
drills.prompt: Two {m} kg blocks on a frictionless track are joined wall–spring–block–spring–block–spring–wall. The outer springs have $k = {k}$ N/m and the middle spring has $k' = {kp}$ N/m. Find the in-phase and out-of-phase normal-mode frequencies (Hz). Then block 1 alone is pulled aside and both blocks are released from rest: find the time (s) until all the motion has passed to block 2. Give 3 significant figures, and keep extra digits in the angular frequencies until the end.
drills.solution:
In phase the middle spring is idle: $\omega_1 = \sqrt{k/m} = \sqrt{{k}/{m}} = {w1:num4}$ rad/s, so $f_1 = \omega_1/2\pi =$ **{f1:sig3} Hz**.

Out of phase each block feels $k + 2k'$: $\omega_2 = \sqrt{({k} + 2 \times {kp})/{m}} = {w2:num4}$ rad/s, so $f_2 =$ **{f2:sig3} Hz**.

The motion passes across in $t = \pi/(\omega_2 - \omega_1) = \pi/{dw:num4} =$ **{tt:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Energy transfer between coupled pendulums
drills.prompt: Two identical pendulums, each {L} m long with a {m} kg bob, are joined at the bobs by a weak spring with $k' = {kp}$ N/m. Using $g = 9.80$ m/s², find the angular frequencies of the in-phase and out-of-phase modes (rad/s, to 4 significant figures). One pendulum is then released while the other hangs still: find the time (s, to 3 significant figures) until the swinging has passed completely to the second pendulum. Use unrounded angular frequencies for the time.
drills.solution:
In phase the spring is idle: $\omega_1 = \sqrt{g/L} = \sqrt{9.80/{L}} =$ **{w1:sig4} rad/s**.

Out of phase the spring adds $2k'/m$: $\omega_2 = \sqrt{9.80/{L} + 2 \times {kp}/{m}} =$ **{w2:sig4} rad/s**.

$\Delta\omega = {dw:num4}$ rad/s, so $t = \pi/\Delta\omega =$ **{tt:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Otto cycle efficiency, temperature and work
drills.prompt: An air-standard Otto cycle ($\gamma = 1.4$, $C_V = \tfrac52R$, $R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K)) has compression ratio {cr}. Air enters at {T1} K and combustion heats it to {T3:dp0} K. Find the efficiency (as a decimal), the temperature at the end of compression (K), and the net work per mole of air per cycle (kJ). Give all three to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$e = 1 - r^{1-\gamma} = 1 - {cr}^{-0.4} =$ **{eff:sig3}**.

Adiabatic compression: $T_2 = T_1r^{\gamma-1} = {T1}({cr})^{0.4} =$ **{T2:sig3} K**.

Heat in at constant volume: $Q_H = C_V(T_3 - T_2) = 20.785({T3:dp0} - {T2:sig4}) = {QH:sig4}$ kJ per mole, so $W = eQ_H =$ **{W:sig3} kJ**.

drills.title: Diesel and Brayton efficiencies
drills.prompt: Using the air-standard model with $\gamma = 1.4$, find (a) the efficiency of a Diesel cycle with compression ratio {cr} and cutoff ratio {rc}, and (b) the efficiency of a Brayton cycle with pressure ratio {rp}. Give both as decimals to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) Cutoff factor: $\dfrac{r_c^{\gamma} - 1}{\gamma(r_c - 1)} = \dfrac{{rc}^{1.4} - 1}{1.4({rc} - 1)} = {fac:sig4}$. Then $e = 1 - \dfrac{{fac:sig4}}{{cr}^{0.4}} =$ **{eD:sig3}**.

(b) $e = 1 - r_p^{-(\gamma - 1)/\gamma} = 1 - {rp}^{-0.2857} =$ **{eB:sig3}**.

drills.title: Entropy of a free expansion by counting
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas expands freely into a vacuum until its volume is {k} times as large, at constant temperature. Counting microstates, find (a) the entropy change in J/K and (b) $\log_{10}$ of the factor by which the number of microstates grows. Use $R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K) and $N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}$, and give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Each of the $N = nN_A$ molecules has {k} times as many places to be, so $\Omega_f/\Omega_i = {k}^N$.

(a) $\Delta S = k_B\ln {k}^N = nR\ln {k} = {n}(8.314)\ln {k} =$ **{dS:sig3} J/K**.

(b) $\log_{10}({k}^N) = N\log_{10}{k} = ({n})(6.022\times10^{23})\log_{10}{k} = \mathbf{{lg:texsci}}$. The number of microstates grows by a factor of 10 raised to that power, which is why the gas never returns to its original volume on its own.

drills.title: Scale height of an isothermal atmosphere
drills.prompt: Treat {gas} as an ideal gas in a still atmosphere at a uniform {T} K. Using the Boltzmann factor, find its scale height $H = RT/(Mg)$ in km and the fraction of its sea-level number density that remains at a height of {y} km. Use $R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K) and $g = 9.8$ m/s², and give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$H = \dfrac{RT}{Mg} = \dfrac{8.314({T})}{({gas:dp3})(9.8)}$ m $=$ **{H:sig3} km**.

The density falls as $e^{-mgy/(k_BT)} = e^{-y/H}$: $e^{-{y}/{H:sig4}} =$ **{frac:sig3}**.

drills.title: Poiseuille flow in a narrow tube
drills.prompt: The fluid is {fl}. It flows smoothly (laminar flow) through a tube of inner radius {Rmm} mm and length {Lcm} cm, driven by a pressure difference of {dPk} kPa. Find the volume flow rate in mL/s and the average flow speed in m/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Poiseuille: $Q = \dfrac{\pi R^4\Delta P}{8\eta L} = \dfrac{\pi({Rm:texsci})^4({dPk}\times10^3)}{8({fl:texsci})({Lcm}\times10^{-2})}$ m³/s $=$ **{Q:sig3} mL/s** (1 mL $= 10^{-6}$ m³).

Average speed: $Q/(\pi R^2) =$ **{vav:sig3} m/s**, half the speed on the axis.

drills.title: Reynolds number of a pipe flow
drills.prompt: The fluid is {fl}. It flows at an average speed of {v} m/s through a pipe of diameter {D} cm. Find the Reynolds number $\text{Re} = \rho vD/\eta$ to 3 significant figures. (Below about 2000 the flow is laminar; above about 3000 it is usually turbulent.)
drills.solution: With $D = {D}$ cm $= {D}\times10^{-2}$ m: $\text{Re} = \dfrac{\rho vD}{\eta} = \dfrac{({rho:sig4})({v})({D}\times10^{-2})}{{eta:sig3}} =$ **{Rey:sig3}**. Compare with about 2000 (laminar below) and about 3000 (usually turbulent above).

drills.title: Stokes settling speed
drills.prompt: A sphere of {gr} with radius {rum} μm settles through still water (density 1000 kg/m³, $\eta = 1.0\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s). Using Stokes' law and $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its terminal speed in mm/s and the Reynolds number $\rho_{\text{water}}v_tD/\eta$ (using the diameter) for that speed. Give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v_t = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho_s - \rho_f)g}{9\eta} = \dfrac{2({rm:texsci})^2({gr:dp0} - 1000)(9.8)}{9(1.0\times10^{-3})} =$ **{vmm:sig3} mm/s**.

$\text{Re} = \dfrac{1000\,v_t(2r)}{1.0\times10^{-3}} = \mathbf{{Rey:texsci}}$, below 1, so Stokes' law applies.
